title: Persist IBKR conid resolutions in the DB so they survive a process restart
description:
Follow-up from a backend-wide caching audit this session. Confirmed via reading the current code before writing this task: `IBKRProvider._conid_cache` (`backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py`) is a plain in-process `dict` with a 24h TTL, added by `backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider` specifically to avoid a `resolve_conid` round trip per ticker per request. That decision's own rationale never weighed restart-survival -- it only considered the per-request-round-trip cost, not the per-process-restart cost.

An IBKR conid-to-ticker mapping is, for all practical purposes, permanent: it only changes on a genuine re-listing/delisting event for that security (rare), not on any regular cadence. Today, every time the backend process restarts (a deploy, a crash, a dev-container rebuild), every single ticker's conid resolution is lost and must be re-fetched live from `/iserver/secdef/search` on its next use -- including the `_resolve_stk_conid` ambiguity-disambiguation logic (`backend-data-provider-timeouts`/`backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider-followups`'s already-hardened primary-US-exchange-preference fix) re-running from scratch for every ticker, every restart.

This is a genuinely new finding, not something previously evaluated or decided against by any closed task this session (checked `docs/tasks/done/backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider*` -- the in-memory-cache decision's rationale doesn't address restart-survival at all).

checklist.step: Design a new `IBKRConidCacheORM` table (ticker as primary key, nullable conid, a `resolved_at` timestamp, and whatever else `_resolve_stk_conid`'s result shape needs to persist -- e.g. the disambiguating exchange/description if useful for debugging a wrong resolution later). Add the Alembic migration. Decide and record (decisions entry) whether a resolved-to-None (genuinely ambiguous) result is also persisted (to avoid re-querying a ticker that's known to need manual disambiguation) or only successful resolutions are cached.

Wire `IBKRProvider.resolve_conid` to check the DB cache before falling back to its existing in-memory cache and then a live `/iserver/secdef/search` call -- in-memory cache stays as the fast path for repeated resolutions within a single process's lifetime, DB cache becomes the fallback that survives a restart. Decide and record (decisions entry) whether the DB cache entry should ever expire/be re-validated (e.g. a long TTL as a safety net against a real re-listing event going unnoticed) or be treated as permanent until manually invalidated.

Handle the concurrent-write case for this new cache table using the same `IntegrityError`/`OperationalError`-catch convention already established in `app/data/cache.py`'s `CachedDataProvider._upsert` (two concurrent requests resolving the same previously-unresolved ticker).

Tests (no live network calls per Testing.md, mocked IBKR HTTP boundary matching `tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py`'s existing convention): DB-cache hit/miss/fallback-to-live paths, the concurrent-write race, and a test confirming a fresh `IBKRProvider` instance (simulating a process restart) reads a previously-resolved conid from the DB without a live `/iserver/secdef/search` call.

decisions.decision: Only a successful (non-null) conid resolution is persisted to the new `IBKRConidCacheORM` table. A genuinely ambiguous/unresolvable ticker (`resolve_conid` returning `None`) is NOT written to this permanent DB cache, even though the existing in-memory `_conid_cache` already caches a `None` result (on its own, much shorter 24h TTL).
decisions.rationale: This table's whole premise is that a successful resolution is effectively permanent and safe to trust indefinitely -- true for a real conid (only a genuine re-listing/delisting event changes it), but NOT true the same way for 'this ticker is ambiguous': the live research behind `_US_PRIMARY_EXCHANGES` (backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider) found a ticker's set of candidate listings can itself change (a feeder-exchange listing appearing/disappearing) in ways this app has no notification of. Permanently freezing a once-ambiguous ticker as unresolvable in the DB would mean a later, now-resolvable state could only ever be picked back up by waiting out the in-memory cache's 24h TTL or restarting the process -- directly undermining the restart-survival property this table exists to provide. Ambiguous tickers are also rare in practice (the primary-US-exchange-preference heuristic already resolves the common multi-listing case), so the cost of occasionally re-querying one live is low. Alternative considered and rejected: caching `None` here too (matching the in-memory cache's behavior) for symmetry and to avoid ever re-querying a known-ambiguous ticker -- rejected because the two caches have very different staleness tolerances (24h vs. effectively forever) and the failure mode of a wrong answer frozen forever is worse than an occasional redundant live call.

decisions.decision: The DB cache entry has no TTL/expiry and is never automatically re-validated -- once a conid is persisted, `resolve_conid` trusts it indefinitely (skipping even `_require_available()`'s gateway-status check) until the row is manually deleted/edited in the database.
decisions.rationale: Matches this task's own `description`: an IBKR conid-to-ticker mapping is, for all practical purposes, permanent, changing only on a rare re-listing/delisting event. Adding a safety-net re-validation TTL (e.g. re-checking against a live gateway every N days) would reintroduce exactly the per-process-restart or per-N-days live round trip this table exists to eliminate, for a staleness risk that's both rare and, when it does happen (an actual re-listing), would surface as a wrong/stale OHLCV fetch an operator can diagnose and fix by deleting the stale row -- not a silent data-corruption risk this app can't recover from. Alternative considered and rejected: a long (e.g. 30-90 day) re-validation TTL as a safety net against an unnoticed re-listing -- rejected as added complexity (a second TTL concept alongside the existing in-memory 24h one) for a risk this task's own description already characterizes as rare enough not to weigh heavily, with a simple manual fix available if it ever does happen.

decisions.decision: `IBKRProvider` gets DB access via an injected `session_factory: Callable[[], Session] | None` (a zero-arg callable that returns a fresh `Session`, e.g. `app.db.session.SessionLocal` itself) rather than a `db: Session` parameter threaded through `resolve_conid` and every one of its callers (`IBKRDataProvider`, `app.api.day_trader_signal`, etc.). `resolve_conid`'s DB-cache read/write each open and close their own short-lived session via this factory.
decisions.rationale: `IBKRProvider` is constructed once as a process-wide singleton (`app.api.dependencies._get_ibkr_provider_singleton`) that outlives any single request's own `Depends(get_db)` session, and `resolve_conid` already has several callers beyond the one (`IBKRDataProvider`) that happens to be constructed per-request with a `db` session available -- `app.api.day_trader_signal._fan_out_per_ticker` calls `provider.resolve_conid(ticker)` directly with no session in scope at all. Threading a `db` parameter through every call site would mean either plumbing a session into call sites that have no natural one (day_trader_signal's per-ticker fan-out) or making the DB cache conditional on which call path was used, inconsistently. A session-factory mirrors the exact pattern `app.api.dependencies.get_data_provider_factory` already established for the same underlying problem (a long-lived/cross-request object that needs its own short-lived DB sessions, opened and closed per use rather than borrowing a request-scoped one it doesn't own). Alternative considered and rejected: adding an optional `db: Session | None` parameter to `resolve_conid` itself, falling back to no DB cache when omitted -- rejected because it would make the DB cache's availability depend on which of several call sites happened to pass one, rather than being a property of the `IBKRProvider` instance itself, and because `IBKRProvider` already can't assume a single request-scoped session exists at all given its singleton lifetime.

decisions.decision: Addressing PR #384's blocking review finding: both `_read_conid_db_cache`'s `SELECT` and `_write_conid_db_cache`'s own pre-commit `SELECT` are now wrapped in the identical `try/except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` handling `_write_conid_db_cache`'s `db.commit()` already had, treating a failed read as a cache miss (`_read_conid_db_cache`, falls through to a live resolution) or as 'no existing row, insert fresh' (`_write_conid_db_cache`'s pre-write check, letting `commit()`'s own existing except-block absorb any resulting duplicate-insert `IntegrityError`) rather than letting either propagate.
decisions.rationale: `app/db/session.py` configures no WAL mode/`busy_timeout`, so SQLite's default whole-file write locking can genuinely raise `OperationalError` on a concurrent *read*, not just a concurrent write's own commit -- the same risk already documented and accepted for `app/data/cache.py`'s cache tables (PR #382's review). `resolve_conid`'s own docstring documents, and `app.api.day_trader_signal`'s `_resolve_and_fetch_legs`/`_fan_out_per_ticker` explicitly rely on, `resolve_conid` never raising anything but `IBKRUnavailableError` -- true before this task by construction (no DB access existed in `resolve_conid` at all), but silently broken by the unwrapped SELECTs this task originally shipped with. Letting either SELECT raise `OperationalError` uncaught would crash an entire batch request (GET /api/watchlist, /api/portfolio, /api/risk, a day-trader endpoint) instead of gracefully degrading just the one ticker -- and could even turn an *already-successfully-resolved* conid (already sitting in `_conid_cache` before the best-effort DB write even runs) into a caller-visible exception, purely because the write's own pre-check read hit transient lock contention. Verified by mutation-testing: temporarily re-raising inside each new except-block reproduces the exact uncaught-`OperationalError` failure the two new regression tests (`test_operational_error_on_db_cache_read_falls_through_to_live_fetch`, `test_operational_error_on_db_cache_write_precommit_read_is_swallowed`) were written to catch, confirming both tests actually exercise this fix rather than passing vacuously. No alternative approach was seriously considered -- this is the same convention the rest of this task (and `app/data/cache.py` before it) already established for the commit-time race; the only question was whether to also apply it to the read side, and the review made clear the answer has to be yes given `resolve_conid`'s documented contract.

decisions.decision: Addressing one of PR #384's non-blocking follow-up findings (also tracked on `backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache-followups`): the optional disambiguating exchange/description column checklist item 1 raised ('whatever else `_resolve_stk_conid`'s result shape needs to persist -- e.g. the disambiguating exchange/description if useful for debugging a wrong resolution later') is deliberately NOT added to `IBKRConidCacheORM`. The final schema stays `ticker`/`conid`/`resolved_at` only.
decisions.rationale: The debugging scenario this column would serve -- 'this ticker resolved to a conid that turns out to be wrong, what made `_resolve_stk_conid` pick it' -- requires the *disambiguation reasoning* (which candidates existed, which one's description matched `_US_PRIMARY_EXCHANGES` and why) at the moment of a specific resolution, not just a label persisted alongside the winning conid; a bare exchange/description string recorded after the fact wouldn't actually explain a wrong pick any better than re-running `resolve_conid` for that ticker live and inspecting the real-time search response would (the live gateway is definitionally the ground truth to debug against, not a stale persisted hint). Persisting it would also mean fabricating a plausible-sounding but unverified value for every one of this PR's own tests that seed a row directly in the DB-cache table (the large majority of `TestResolveConidDbCache`) rather than going through a live-like `_resolve_stk_conid` call, which would make those seeded rows look more informative than they actually are. Weighed against that: an extra nullable column costs little, but 'little cost, no concretely identified debugging benefit' isn't a reason to add schema surface -- if a real wrong-resolution incident is ever investigated and this data would have helped, that's the point to add the column with a real use case driving its shape, rather than speculatively now. Alternative considered and rejected: adding it now as a nullable `TEXT` column capturing the raw matched search-result `description` string -- rejected for the reasons above, but left as an easy follow-up if a concrete debugging need for it ever actually arises.

comments.summary: Round 2: the round-1 blocking finding is correctly fixed. Both `_read_conid_db_cache`'s SELECT and `_write_conid_db_cache`'s pre-commit SELECT are now wrapped in `try/except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)`, matching the existing commit-time handling. Verified by mutation-testing both new except-blocks myself (temporarily re-raising inside each): `test_operational_error_on_db_cache_read_falls_through_to_live_fetch` fails without the read-path guard, `test_operational_error_on_db_cache_write_precommit_read_is_swallowed` fails without the write-path pre-commit guard; both pass with the guards restored and the working tree diffed clean afterward. Also independently traced the 'spurious pre-commit-read failure while a row genuinely already exists' scenario the dispatch asked about: since the fallback path always constructs a brand-new transient `IBKRConidCacheORM(ticker=cache_key)` and `db.add()`s it (never an `UPDATE`), a collision with an actually-existing row surfaces as a primary-key `IntegrityError` on `commit()`, which the pre-existing commit-time except-block already catches and discards correctly -- reproduced with a standalone scratch script seeding an existing row, forcing the pre-commit SELECT to raise, and confirming the real row (not the spurious write) survives untouched. No bug found in this path.

Round 2: all 3 round-1 non-blocking findings were folded into this PR and verified accurate -- Backend.md's new subsection correctly describes the DB-cache fallback/session_factory pattern, `test_singleton_wires_session_factory_to_sessionlocal` correctly asserts `provider._session_factory is SessionLocal` against the real `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton` wiring, and a new `decisions` entry explains the deliberate omission of a disambiguation-debug column. All verified by reading the code each references.

Non-blocking, new in round 2: `_read_conid_db_cache`'s SELECT-wrapped-in-try/except and `_write_conid_db_cache`'s pre-commit SELECT-wrapped-in-try/except are near-identical blocks duplicated across the two methods (query by `cache_key`, catch `(IntegrityError, OperationalError)`, log, fall back to a miss/no-row). A small shared helper would avoid the two copies drifting later. Pure reuse/simplification observation, not a bug -- tracked on the followups task.

review.notes: Round 2 re-review (PR #384, branch task/backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache, superseding the round-1 needs_work at bf19cd8d). Full backend suite: 1598 passed (ran twice, deterministic). Coverage: 100% line/branch (90% gate), `app/data/ibkr_provider.py` itself at 100%. ruff and mypy both clean. `scripts/validate_tasks.py` clean (366 task files, no invariant violations). `backend/openapi.json` re-exported locally and diffed clean -- no API route/schema touched by this PR, consistent with its description. Alembic: single head (`c8216d30fc10`), migration file correct (create/drop `ibkr_conid_cache` with `ticker` primary key). Mutation-tested both new regression tests directly (see comment above) -- both fail without their respective fix, pass with it, clean diff after restoring. Independently traced the write-path 'spurious read failure racing a genuinely-existing row' scenario raised by the dispatch instruction: confirmed via a standalone scratch reproduction that the resulting duplicate INSERT correctly collides on the `ticker` primary key and is absorbed by the pre-existing commit-time IntegrityError handler -- no silent corruption or lost write. Confirmed `resolve_conid`'s 'never raises anything but IBKRUnavailableError' contract holds end-to-end by reading `_require_available`/`_request`'s own exception surface (unchanged by this PR) and `app/api/day_trader_signal.py`'s caller, which explicitly catches only `IBKRUnavailableError`. No frontend changes in this PR -- browser walkthrough and `e2e-test` skill explicitly skipped, no UI surface. `backend/fintrade.db.pre-migration-fix.bak` left untouched; pre-existing unrelated git stash (`task/indicator-elder-ray` entry) left untouched; no live IBKR gateway call made or depended on by any test (all HTTP/`_request`/`get_gateway_status` boundaries mocked, matching this module's existing convention) despite `backend/.env`'s `FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED=true`. One new non-blocking finding (duplicated SELECT-wrapping try/except pattern between the two DB-cache methods, a reuse/simplification nit) added to `backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache-followups`'s checklist. No `pr_decision` was present on this task to clear.
